html:
A football code that began in Melbourne in 1859, when the Melbourne Football Club wrote down its first rules. It is now the most watched sport in Australia.

The game grew out of the boom town of the gold rush. Tom Wills, a star cricketer, wanted a winter game to keep cricketers fit. He and three others drafted ten short rules in May 1859. Games were played on cricket grounds, which is why the field is a large oval, and the Melbourne Cricket Ground is still its home.

Teams of 18 kick, catch ("mark") and punch the ball by hand. There is no offside, so players can be anywhere on the field. Some writers think Wills drew on Marn Grook, a ball game played by Aboriginal people in Victoria; historians still argue about the link.

A league of clubs formed in Victoria in 1896 and became the national Australian Football League in 1990. The game spread across the southern and western states, while rugby kept its hold in Sydney and Brisbane.
sum: A football code that began in Melbourne in 1859, when the Melbourne Football Club wrote down its first rules. It is now the most watched sport in Australia.
